0.0.n: A familiar, blunt form of あなた that can sound confrontational.

0.2.n: Adds doubt or emphasis to the question about identity.

0.3.n: 朱 is the surname in the name 朱慧月.

0.4.n: 慧 is the first character of the given name 慧月, not a separate word here.

0.5.n: 月 completes the given name 慧月; it does not mean moon independently here.

0.6.n: Plain form of です, linking the listener to the name.

0.7.n: Adds insistence; together, よな asks for confirmation of something the speaker expects to be true.

0.8.n: Sentence-ending な seeks agreement here, with a rough, familiar tone.

1.0.n: 次 plus に sets the time for the hypothetical action.

1.1.n: 玲 is the first character of the name 玲琳, not a separate word here.

1.2.n: 琳 completes the name 玲琳.

1.3.n: Links 玲琳 to 猿真似, identifying the person being copied.

1.4.n: Literally monkey imitation, this noun disparages copying someone without originality.

1.5.n: Marks 猿真似 as what the listener might do.

1.6.n: する plus なら makes a condition; the consequence follows in the next line.

2.0.n: Names the body part to be severed in the threat.

2.1.n: Marks 首 as the target of 刎ねる.

2.2.n: 刎 is the first part of 刎ねる, the verb used for cutting off a head.

2.3.n: ねる completes 刎ねる; it is not an independent verb here.

2.4.n: Marks the preceding threat as the content of what was said.

2.5.n: Adds the beheading threat as another thing the speaker says they communicated.

2.6.n: Past plain form of 告げる, a somewhat formal verb for informing or declaring.

2.7.n: After a past verb, はず expresses confident expectation that the action already happened.

2.8.n: Completes はずだ, presenting the speaker's expectation as a firm assertion.

2.9.n: Leaves the contrast unstated, creating a pointed challenge rather than a neutral question.

3.0.n: A very deferential acknowledgment, using the polite past form of かしこまる.

4.0.n: A self-deprecating description suggesting the speaker lacks refinement or ability.

4.1.n: Connects the descriptive word ふつつか directly to the noun 悪女.

4.2.n: Refers to a wicked woman; the speaker applies this label to herself.

4.3.n: Begins ではございます, a very polite way to link the speaker with 悪女.

4.4.n: Highlights the admitted description before が introduces a contrasting commitment.

4.5.n: ございます makes the statement much more formal than ordinary です.

4.6.n: Connects the self-deprecating description to the promise that follows.

4.8.n: A literary or forceful word for oneself, referring to the speaker here.

4.9.n: Marks 己 as the standard that the behavior should match.

4.10.n: Past form of 見合う describing 行動; here it means suitable, not a completed past action.

4.11.n: With をいたします, this noun describes how the speaker promises to act.

4.12.n: Marks 行動 as what the speaker will carry out.

4.13.n: Polite form of いたす, the humble alternative to する, lowering the speaker's own action respectfully.

0.lit: You really are Shu Keigetsu, right?
0.tip: だよな seeks confirmation insistently rather than asking a neutral question.

1.lit: Next time, if you do a mindless imitation of Reirin,
1.tip: なら makes this a condition whose threatened consequence comes in the next line.

2.lit: I should have also told you that I would sever your neck, but?
2.tip: 告げたはずだが pointedly reminds the listener of a warning the speaker believes was already given.

3.tip: かしこまりました acknowledges instructions with much more deference than わかりました.

4.lit: Although I am an inept villainess, I will undertake conduct befitting myself.
4.tip: ございます and いたします make her self-description and promise exceptionally polite.
